exact_missing_items: That split keeps teaching implementers that `TierChanged` and `UserInteractionRequired` are the primary operational truth even though the runtime/storage owner docs have already moved to canonical event and projection families.
The Slint-facing `GraphNodeUI` and callbacks still preserve the same assumptions:
The `Progress` tab is already correctly identified as widget-composed, but its default widget contract is still strongly tier-era.
The blocker bundle remains materially blocked, but the next useful stage is now `Ledger Condenser`, not another Audit Mode sweep.
The current unresolved blocker inventory therefore remains at eight blocker families, nineteen affected docs, and fifty underlying evidence refs.
The duplicated `Crosswalk.md` numbering is not cosmetic. It undermines `ContractRef` stability and gateable traceability.

The duplicated runtime-recovery addendum means the gate doc now has same-file canon duplication similar to the problems already logged in `Crosswalk.md`, `human-in-the-loop.md`, and `storage-plan.md`.
The effective-resolution record is close to the rewrite direction, but it still lacks the newer identity layers already established elsewhere:
The file still treats tier boundaries as the approval scope anchor, while newer runtime canon requires blocked-episode identity anchored by run/node/blocked sequence.
The graph approval commands do not currently have one stable args contract even before considering the broader runtime-model rewrite.
